plan: To preserve capital, we will sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% and CRWD to 10% to reduce concentration and meet mandate limits.
Increase QQQI to 25% to favor income and stability.
Buy PANW at 5% as a top-quality AI/Software name.
This plan aims for steady, low-drawdown performance with a focus on capital preservation.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdown. However, potential upside is also limited.

plan: For a balanced approach, trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leverage.
Reduce SPY to 25% and CRWD to 10% to meet concentration limits.
Add PANW at 5% and LRCX at 5% as high-scoring quality tech names.
This strategy blends broad index exposure with quality tech and controlled leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding quality tech. Expect moderate drawdowns with potential for solid growth.

plan: For aggressive growth, increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the mandate, while adding to CRWD at 14% to press what is working.
Buy LRCX at 7% and PANW at 7% as top-scoring scanner setups.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of higher potential drawdowns and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: To prioritize income, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% for steady monthly distributions.
Trim SPY to 20% for broad index stability.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to reduce high-beta single name exposure.
This plan focuses on low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta names, favoring income-generating ETFs. While aiming for low drawdown and reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable.
